title: Review: Common atmospheric pollutants and their sources; Using the Earth's resources and obtaining potable water
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms: 4.10.1-c08, 4.10.1-c10, 4.9.3-c14, 4.9.3-c13. Clues: 4.10.1-c08 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.10.1-c10 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.9.3-c14 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.9.3-c13 written for the game from the bank's definition. Questions: 4.9.3-q13, 4.10.1-q02, 4.9.3-q12, 4.10.1-q10, 4.9.3-q11, 4.10.1-q03, 4.9.3-q14, 4.10.1-q04, 4.9.3-q09, 4.10.1-q05, 4.9.3-q10, 4.10.1-q07. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Potable water
items.clue: Water that is safe to drink.

items.label: Fresh water
items.clue: Water with low levels of dissolved substances.

items.label: Respiratory problems
items.clue: Damage to or irritation of the breathing system in humans.

items.label: Acid rain
items.clue: Caused when sulfur dioxide or oxides of nitrogen dissolve in water in the air.

questions.stem: Particulate levels in the air over a city rise year after year, and less sunlight now reaches the streets. Why do particulates have this effect?

options.text: They are suspended solids that block sunlight
They are a gas that soaks up light and heat
They trap warmth near the Earth's surface
They have thinned the ozone layer above us

questions.explanation: Particulates are tiny solids suspended in the air. They reflect and absorb sunlight on its way in, so less reaches the surface: global dimming.

questions.stem: Natural resources are supplemented by agriculture. Which list of products does the specification give for these resources?

options.text: Warmth, shelter, transport and heavy machinery
Food, timber, clothing and fuels are all provided
Food and clothing only, since fuels are all synthetic
Only timber and other farmed plant materials

questions.explanation: The specification states that natural resources, supplemented by agriculture, provide food, timber, clothing and fuels.

questions.stem: Particulates in the atmosphere cause health problems for humans. What other effect does the specification give for particulates?

options.text: They add to global warming
They cause global dimming
They cause acid rain damage
They destroy the ozone layer

questions.explanation: The specification states that particulates cause global dimming and health problems for humans.

questions.stem: A river sample contains 12 mg/dm3 of dissolved solids; sea water contains about 35 000 mg/dm3. How do these compare?

options.text: Sea water contains roughly three times as much
Sea water contains only about twice as much
The two values are of a similar order of magnitude
Sea water contains three orders of magnitude more

questions.explanation: 35 000 divided by 12 is roughly 3000, which is a factor of about a thousand.

questions.stem: As well as causing acid rain, sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen affect people directly. What effect on humans does the specification give?

options.text: They cause problems with breathing
They cause dimming of sunlight
They make a hole in the ozone layer
They cause skin damage from sunlight

questions.explanation: The specification states that sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen cause respiratory problems in humans.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly matches a natural product with the synthetic product that can replace it?

options.text: Natural cotton fibre is replaced by farmed wool fibre
Natural rubber from latex is replaced by iron and steel
Natural rubber from latex replaced by synthetic rubber
Farmed timber is replaced by synthetic wood made from trees

questions.explanation: Latex tapped from rubber trees is a natural product and synthetic rubber, made industrially, supplements and replaces it.

questions.stem: Stonework on a city building is being eaten away, and tests show the rain falling there is acidic. Which rise in air pollution explains this damage?

options.text: More sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen
More carbon dioxide from the burning fuel
More carbon monoxide from car exhausts
More particulates from sooty chimneys

questions.explanation: The specification gives sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen as the causes of acid rain, which is what attacks the stonework.

questions.stem: Finite resources from the Earth, oceans and atmosphere are processed. What does the specification say this provides?

options.text: Renewable supplies that will never be used up
Only fuels and metals dug straight out of the rock
Metal ores that are then recycled indefinitely by us
Energy and the materials that people can use

questions.explanation: The specification states that finite resources are processed to provide energy and materials.

questions.stem: Carbon monoxide leaks from a faulty boiler into a house. Why is this so dangerous?

options.text: It has a sharp smell that people learn to ignore
It turns the water vapour in the room into acid
It is toxic, and colourless and odourless so hard to spot
It is explosive and can set the whole room alight

questions.explanation: The specification states that carbon monoxide is a toxic gas and that it is colourless and odourless, so it is not easily detected.

questions.stem: What makes a resource finite rather than renewable?

options.text: It cannot be recycled after it has been used
It is used up more quickly than it is replaced
It is buried underground rather than grown
It cannot be used more than a single time

questions.explanation: A finite resource is not being replaced, or is replaced far more slowly than it is used, so it will run out.

questions.stem: Which pollutants does the specification name as the causes of acid rain?

options.text: Carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide
Particulates and oxides of nitrogen
Carbon monoxide and unburned hydrocarbons
Sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen

questions.explanation: The specification states that sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen cause respiratory problems in humans and cause acid rain.

questions.stem: Which of these best describes sustainable development?

options.text: Development that uses none of the natural resources of the Earth at all
Development that meets the needs of future generations rather than those of people now
Development in which every material that industry uses is recycled afterwards
Development that meets the needs of today without compromising future ones

questions.explanation: This is the definition given in the specification.
